_README: CANONICAL measured figures. Every gas or ratio claim in prose (CLAUDE.md,
README.md, docs/, NatSpec, commit messages) must agree with this file, and
this file is enforced by Measurements.test.js, which RE-MEASURES each entry
rather than trusting it.
Why this exists: three strategic conclusions in this project were reversed
because a number was wrong, and each reversal was then APPENDED next to the
wrong claim instead of replacing it. A later reader — including a later
session — met the stale claim first and re-derived from it. The 'skip t=16'
decision was made from a >100M figure that was already known to be an
artefact. Prose cannot be kept in sync by discipline alone; this file can be
kept in sync by CI.
HOW TO MEASURE (the three mistakes that produced the reversals):
1. A gasLimit above 2^24 is REJECTED BEFORE EXECUTION (EIP-7825). A
rejection is not an out-of-gas. Always confirm the call actually ran.
2. estimateGas over-provisions nested calls by ~3x (63/64 rule per frame).
Measure gasUsed of a SENT transaction; for a view function, binary
search the smallest passing gasLimit.
3. In a RATIO, shared overhead must cancel. Two single external calls both
carry the 21,000 transaction base, which inflates the smaller one and
understates the ratio. Measure marginally: gas(n+1) - gas(n).
Tolerance is 3%: compiler and fixture regeneration move these slightly, a
real regression moves them much more.

nonce_transition_verify.what: BatchRegistryV7.submitNonceTransition with ONE update — the nonce accumulator's whole on-chain cost, dominated by its own verifyRecursive. Constant in N.
nonce_transition_verify.how: contracts/test/BatchRegistryV7Accumulator.test.js sends the transaction and reads gasUsed. Fixture: nonce_accumulator_e2e.json (cargo test write_nonce_accumulator_fixture -- --ignored).
nonce_transition_verify.note: THIS NUMBER REFUTES § A-4's CENTRAL CLAIM in the separate-proof form. Against the mapping's measured 12,085 gas per RETURNING sender it only pays above ~563 senders, and one transaction admits ~172. So the accumulator as a SEPARATE proof does not reach break-even — it is dearer than the mapping at every N the cap allows.
nonce_transition_verify.and_it_does_not_fit_with_a_batch: 14,663,950 (v7_tree_submitBatch) + 6,813,715 = 21,477,665 against a 16,777,216 cap. The first design took the batch bundles in the same call and reverted; that is how this was measured rather than assumed. Hence submitNonceTransition is its own transaction.
nonce_transition_verify.what_would_fix_it: Fold the nonce statement into the batch proof as a further component of the tree's root node (nonce_update_t8_air — not a merkle_path_t8_air path group, which would reopen the A-4 sibling hole), so it rides the two verifyRecursive calls already being paid for instead of adding a third. The separate proof was recorded as 'simpler and cheaper'; only the first half was true.
nonce_transition_verify.remeasured: 2026-10-08, on the two-lane nonce_update_t8_air (TECH_DEBT § A-4: the two-path construction let a link's new leaf use different siblings from its old one, i.e. replay). The two-path figure was 6,882,057; the conclusion is unchanged.

nonce_transition_marginal.what: Marginal gas per additional update in submitNonceTransition, measured 1 -> 25 updates.
nonce_transition_marginal.how: Same test. Marginally, so the ~6.9M constant cancels.
nonce_transition_marginal.note: STORAGE is O(1) — one slot holds the whole replay state whatever N is — but this is still HIGHER than the mapping's 12,085 per returning sender, so the accumulator loses on the marginal as well as on the constant. Two contributors, both addressable: nonceStatementBinding concatenates with abi.encodePacked in a loop, which is O(n^2) in memory, and a 25-update statement has a much larger inner trace than a 1-update one: the fixture's inner treeDepth is 13 against 8 (25 two-lane updates at D = 8 is 4,400 rows; it was 14 against 9 on the two-path form). This note said 'log 10 vs 9' until 2026-10-08 — wrong, and it matters: the same depth growth applies to whichever tree-root node carries the nonce paths once they are folded into the batch.
nonce_transition_marginal.remeasured: 2026-10-08, two-lane component: half the rows, twice the columns per update. Was 21,083 on the two-path construction.

outer_recursion_verify_t8.what: VFRI11 verify of the OUTER recursion trace (87 cols, log=14, inner n_queries=20)

outer_recursion_verify_t16.what: VFRI12 verify of the same outer trace — 96% of the cap, which is why a fully t=16 recursion does not fit

v7_tree_submitBatch.what: BatchRegistryV7.submitBatch finalizing a BATCH of signatures from the aggregation tree's two roots, at production n_queries=20 (130-bit FRI).
v7_tree_submitBatch.how: cargo test write_tree_recursive_bundles_fixture -- --ignored; then contracts/test/BatchRegistryV7TreeE2E.test.js sends the tx and reads gasUsed.
v7_tree_submitBatch.note: merkleRoot here is R, the membership root DERIVED from the proofs and used as the Fiat-Shamir seed, with txListRoot carried alongside as the (attested, unproved) transaction-list commitment. Constant in N: the root node's shape is a fixed point, so two signatures measure the same as many. The fixture's fold count is derived from each root's DEPTH, not the leaves' — a tree root sits at depth 15/14 where a V23 group sits at 10/8, so inheriting the leaves' 6 folds put 512 last-layer evaluations on chain instead of 16 and the call reverted. Measuring the outer trace alone and inferring the total was the error.

v7_sender_marginal_cold.what: Marginal gas per additional FIRST-TIME sender in BatchRegistryV7.submitBatchWithNonces, measured 10 -> 25 senders.
v7_sender_marginal_cold.how: contracts/test/V7SenderCostProbe.test.js sends batches at 1/10/25 senders on fresh registries and differences the gasUsed, so the ~14.7M shared batch cost and the 21,000 tx base cancel.
v7_sender_marginal_cold.note: FIRST-TIME: a fresh registry means every sender writes a ZERO slot, so this carries SSTORE_SET (20,000) + the cold-slot surcharge (2,100). USE THIS FOR THE CEILING — how many senders fit one transaction must hold in the worst case, a batch of all-new senders. Do NOT use it for break-even; see v7_sender_marginal_warm. GROWS with n (26,065 at 1->10) because of the O(n^2) duplicate scan.
v7_sender_marginal_cold.corrected: Was named `v7_sender_marginal` and used for BOTH the ceiling and break-even. The harness comment beside it already said 'a warm senderNonces slot costs less than a cold one', but the consequence never reached ROADMAP § 1.5 — so prose drifted from a number inside the file that exists to prevent exactly that. Renamed so the name states which case it measures.

v7_sender_marginal_warm.what: Marginal gas per additional RETURNING sender — one that appeared in an earlier batch, so its senderNonces slot is already non-zero.
v7_sender_marginal_warm.how: contracts/test/V7SenderCostProbe.test.js on NonceLoopHarness (contracts/src/test/), which carries BatchRegistryV7's nonce block verbatim. Two calls into ONE harness: the first warms the slots, the second is measured. The real contract cannot produce this — a second batch needs a second merkleRoot, finalizedBatches rejects a repeat, and a different root needs different cross-bound proofs.
v7_sender_marginal_warm.note: USE THIS FOR BREAK-EVEN — it is what a running system pays for almost every sender; the first-time cost is paid once per sender ever. The difference from the cold figure is 17,100 gas, which is EXACTLY SSTORE_SET (20,000) - SSTORE_RESET (2,900).
v7_sender_marginal_warm.harness_validated: A harness measured only against itself measures nothing. The same test cross-checks it against the real contract on the TWO points the real contract CAN produce before using its third: cold 29,185 vs 28,777 (1.4%) and warm-within-one-transaction 12,946 vs 12,538 (3.3%), both inside a 5% bound. If V7's loop changes and the harness's does not, that check fails.
v7_sender_marginal_warm.consequence: The correction moves the numbers a lot and does NOT overturn the conclusion. Compared consistently at the steady-state marginal: break-even needs N > 359 and one transaction holds ~172 senders, so break-even stays OUTSIDE the ceiling: on these figures the mapping cannot reach break-even within one transaction. This note used to add that the nonce accumulator (§ A-4) is the lever that does — refuted on 2026-10-05 for the separate-proof form, see nonce_transition_verify. What changes is the margin — the gap narrows from ~8.4x (607 needed against 72 reachable, both on the cold figure) to ~2.1x. The worst-case ceiling, which is what a safety limit must use, stays at ~71.

v8_stack_pre_run_check_2026_10_08.what: The 2026-10-10 public-testnet path, re-run end to end against a standalone `npx hardhat node` after the 2026-10-08 Rust changes (A-6 fix, A-4 two-lane component, Ш2/Ш3 nonce folding behind *_with_nonce wrappers). deploy_v8.sh --network localnode, then python3 -m testnet.e2e --stack v8 --txs 2, with the PyO3 extension rebuilt from the current tree.

sepolia_v8_first_public_run.network: Ethereum Sepolia (chainId 11155111) — the FIRST run on a public network
sepolia_v8_first_public_run.what: testnet.e2e --stack v8 --txs 2: real ML-DSA-65 signatures -> V23 -> aggregation tree over both -> recursion -> BatchRegistryV7.submitBatchWithNonces, ONE transaction, 2 first-time senders. finalized=True.
sepolia_v8_first_public_run.vs_local: +585,977 (+4.0%) over v8_stack_pre_run_check_2026_10_08 (14,726,046, standalone hardhat node). Local runs of the same command vary by ~10k (fresh keys), so this is not calldata.
sepolia_v8_first_public_run.cause: PARTLY ESTABLISHED by sepolia_fixture_replay (2026-11-18): the same fixture calldata costs +2.96% on Sepolia, so ~434.7k of the gap is the network's gas schedule. The remaining ~151k sits in the nonce/storage path (2 first-time senders cost 213,285 there vs 62,008 locally) — see that entry.
sepolia_v8_first_public_run.consequence: Headroom under the 16,777,216 per-tx cap is 1,465,193 on Sepolia against ~2.05M locally, so the worst-case sender ceiling (first-time senders at 28,777 each) drops from ~71 to ~50 there. The local figures in `entries` are NOT changed: they are what the test suite re-measures.

sepolia_fixture_replay.what: The FIXTURE's tree batch (tree_recursive_bundles_e2e.json) — byte-for-byte the calldata `entries.v7_tree_submitBatch` re-measures locally — sent with BatchRegistryV7.submitBatch to the same registry. No senders.
sepolia_fixture_replay.vs_local: +434,700 (+2.96%) over 14,664,038, the same calldata on Hardhat today (cancun, prague and osaka give the identical figure). Same bytes, same contract: this part of the gap is the NETWORK's gas schedule, not a proof.
sepolia_fixture_replay.and_the_rest: It does not explain all of the first run's +585,977. Subtracting the two Sepolia transactions isolates the nonce part (2 first-time senders, submitBatchWithNonces vs submitBatch): 213,285 on Sepolia against 62,008 locally — +151,277, ~3.4x, where a uniform ~3% would give ~64k. Fresh-proof variance is ~10k locally, so nearly all of it sits in the sender/storage path. Likely reading: Sepolia's schedule prices new storage writes far above the local one. That is an inference from two numbers, NOT a direct measurement.
sepolia_fixture_replay.why_it_matters: If storage writes cost ~3-4x more, a first-time sender on the mapping path costs ~100k instead of 28,777 — the per-tx sender ceiling falls from ~70 to ~16, and the nonce accumulator (Ф3.2), which removes those writes, gains correspondingly. ROADMAP § 1.5's economics would need re-deriving on that schedule.
sepolia_fixture_replay.next: Measure it directly: marginal sender cost on Sepolia (batches with different numbers of first-time senders, differenced), as V7SenderCostProbe does locally.

sepolia_sender_cost.what: Marginal per-sender cost on Sepolia, same fixed sequence as the local baseline: real BatchRegistryV7 on fresh registries with 0/1/5/10 first-time senders, NonceLoopHarness first-time 5/10/25 and returning 10/25. Raw figures and every tx hash: contracts/test/fixtures/sender_cost_sepolia.json; local: sender_cost_local.json.

first_time_sender.note: The delta is EXACTLY 88,020 in all three ranges measured (real 1->5, real 5->10, harness 10->25): a constant per-sender repricing, not noise. Harness vs real contract on Sepolia: 0.14%.

new_storage_slot_premium.how: first-time delta minus returning delta: 88,020 - 7,200. A write that CREATES a slot costs ~80.8k more on Sepolia; cold minus returning is 97,920 there vs 17,100 locally (5.7x).

batch_without_senders.explained: Finalization creates 5 storage slots (finalizedBatches, batchTimestamps, both commitment maps, batchTxListRoots): 5 x 80,820 = 404,100 of the 434,700. The residual 30,600 is 0.21% of the batch. So the proof VERIFICATION itself — the Poseidon2 / FRI / recursion work — costs the same on Sepolia to within ~0.2%: the whole gap is state creation.

sepolia_sender_cost.first_public_run_reconciled: 15,312,023 (2026-11-17) vs fixture batch 15,098,738 + 2 first-time senders 113,951 + 113,520 = 15,326,209: -14,186 (-0.09%), inside the ~±15k proof-to-proof variance seen locally. The +4.0% of the first run is fully accounted for.

code_deposit.note: +8,290,610 over 5,918 runtime bytes: deployed code costs ~7-8x more per byte (local deposit 200/byte). ESTIMATE from this one contract, linear in size: QLSAVerifierVFRI11 (21,993 B) would need ~35.6M to deploy today — over the 16,777,216 per-tx cap, so it could NOT be redeployed on this schedule; QLSAVerifierRecursive (9,477 B) ~15.4M, just under. The deployed copies (2026-10-11) predate this pricing and are unaffected.

sepolia_sender_cost.reading: The pattern — new storage slots ~5x, new code ~7-8x, updates to existing state and computation essentially unchanged — is that of a state-creation repricing. Which network upgrade Sepolia runs could not be checked from the development environment; whether mainnet adopts the same schedule decides how much of this applies there.

economics_on_this_schedule.break_even_first_time: UNREACHABLE: a new sender (117,205) costs more than the 52,944 of calldata a signature saves
economics_on_this_schedule.note: Both against the mainnet calldata figure (52,944 per signature); local: ceilings ~71/~172, break-even ~618/~359.
